zh: 一个位置最终是否开启，只取决于覆盖它的操作次数的奇偶性。闭区间 [l, r] 的翻转等价于在 l 和 r+1 两处各放一个翻转事件：某位置之前（含）的事件数与覆盖它的操作数奇偶相同。端点可达 INT_MAX，不能按最大编号开数组逐位模拟。
把所有 2n 个事件排序（保留重复值，不能去重）。初始全关，每经过一个事件状态翻转，所以排序后第 0、1 个事件之间、第 2、3 个事件之间……就是开启段 [a, b)。相同坐标的两个事件只组成空段，自然体现偶数次抵消。
开启段 a..b−1 的编号和是 (a+b−1)(b−a)/2，逐对累加即可。事件多达一千多万个，参考用两趟稳定的 16 位基数排序（先低 16 位再高 16 位）。r+1 最大是 2147483648，要用无符号 32 位或更宽的类型；求和时先提升到 64 位，总和最大 2305843008139952128。
en: Whether a position ends up on depends only on the parity of the number of operations covering it. Toggling the closed interval [l, r] is equivalent to placing one toggle event at l and one at r+1: the number of events at or before a position has the same parity as the number of operations covering it. Endpoints reach INT_MAX, so you cannot allocate an array up to the largest index and simulate.

Sort all 2n events, keeping duplicates (do not deduplicate). Everything starts off and the state flips at each event, so after sorting, the stretch between events 0 and 1, between events 2 and 3, and so on, is an on-segment [a, b). Two events at the same coordinate form an empty segment, which naturally expresses the cancellation of an even number of toggles.

The index sum of the on-segment a..b−1 is (a+b−1)(b−a)/2; add it up pair by pair. There can be more than ten million events, and the reference uses two stable 16-bit radix passes (low 16 bits first, then high 16 bits). r+1 can be 2147483648, so use an unsigned 32-bit or wider type; widen to 64 bits for the sum, whose maximum is 2305843008139952128.

explanationEn:
## Original rules, range and return-value adaptation

The pinned original fastprep/Expedia/expedia-calculate-the-sum.md states in full: switches are numbered consecutively from 1, and all start off. Each operation gives left and right endpoints and toggles every switch in the closed interval once; at the end, find the sum of the indices of all switches that are on. It is not the number of switches that are on, nor the union of the intervals covered by the operations. Overlapping operations cancel by parity. The original has no examples; the three public examples are all constructed by this site.

The original constraints section contains only an emoticon and no numeric upper bound; the parameters are explicitly Java int n and int[][] operations. This site openly interprets valid indices by type as 1≤l≤r≤2147483647 and does not invent smaller bounds on endpoints or the number of operations. n is treated as a non-negative operation count; n=0 with answer 0 is this site's explicit mathematical extension for no operations, and it does not claim the original gives a lower bound on n. Standard input is n followed by n pairs of endpoints, accepting whitespace separation, LF/CRLF and EOF right after the last number. All inputs are still bounded by the existing 32MiB standard transfer budget; n=8388606 with every line being 1 1, in canonical LF encoding, takes exactly 33554432 bytes, which is a derivation from the budget rather than a constraint from the source.

The original int return type cannot cover this complete type domain; for example, a single [1,2147483647] gives 2305843008139952128. This site outputs the exact mathematical integer, with no truncation or modulo, and explicitly widens the result to 64 bits. Every position that can be on lies in 1..INT_MAX, so this value is also the largest answer over the whole domain, and signed 64 bits suffice. The original edited version allocated an array up to the largest index, which cannot cover INT_MAX; this site does not reuse it to quietly shrink the domain.

Public constructed examples: after operations [1,3] and [2,4], only 1 and 4 are on, for a sum of 5; two [2,5] cancel completely, for a sum of 0; a single [2147483647,2147483647] gives a sum of 2147483647. These are not presented as original source examples.

## Approach

Turn each closed interval [l,r] into two parity toggle events, l and r+1. Sort all events, keeping duplicates. A switch's state flips once at each event, starting from off, so the adjacent event pairs 0/1, 2/3 and so on give the on-segments [a,b). Two equal events form an empty segment contributing 0; this naturally keeps the cancellation effect of an even number of toggles.

The index sum of the on-segment a..b−1 is (a+b−1)(b−a)/2. Accumulate it pair by pair, without visiting switches one by one or allocating an array up to the largest index. The reference sorts the uint32 events with two stable 16-bit radix passes: first the low 16 bits, then the high 16 bits. Each pass first counts and converts counts into starting offsets, then scatters into the other array in the original order, which guarantees stability.

## Proof of correctness

For any position x, an operation [l,r] toggles it exactly when l≤x<r+1. After replacing it with the two events l and r+1, the total number of events up to x has the same parity as the number of operations covering x, so both representations produce exactly the same switch states.

After sorting the events, nothing changes state between adjacent events; the initial state is off, and each event flips it. So the stretch from an even-numbered event to the next event is on, and the stretch before the next pair is off. Duplicate coordinates contain no switch; pairing gives an empty segment, or consecutive flips at the same coordinate, and keeping them correctly expresses parity. The on-segments do not overlap, and their union is exactly the set of all on positions. Summing each segment as an arithmetic series and adding them gives exactly the target index sum.

The stable low-digit sort orders values by their low bits within equal high bits; the second, stable high-bit pass keeps that low-bit order, so the final result is in full 32-bit numeric order, satisfying the pairing argument above.

## Complexity and full input budget

The two radix passes and the summation take O(n+65536) time and O(n+65536) space. Two uint32 arrays of 2n elements take 16n bytes in total; at the largest transferable operation count 8388606 that is 134217696 bytes, plus a 262144-byte count table and a little runtime overhead, below 256MiB. Parsing is streamed, with no separate input string or operation array. The two largest inputs are tested sequentially, without running large processes concurrently.

r+1 is computed in uint32, at most 2147483648; it must not be added in signed int first. For the sum, endpoints are first widened to uint64: each segment's product is at most 2147483648×2147483647, and the final total is at most 2305843008139952128, with no overflow anywhere. Zero operations produce no events and output 0.

## Independent verification

The small-domain oracle maintains the on/off state of every switch directly, toggles position by position, then sums the indices of the on positions; it exhausts indices 1..4 with 0..4 valid intervals, 11111 sets in total. The 163 unique oracle cases include random small inputs and full endpoint boundaries. The medium-scale oracle XORs events into a dictionary one by one, sorts the distinct coordinates and scans by state, without using the reference's radix sort or direct pairing. At least 35 formal cases cover duplicates, crossings, touching, nesting, INT_MAX endpoints, 0 operations and every line ending. Two inputs close to 32MiB are, respectively, the maximum number of operations on a repeated single point (cancelled by an even count) and shuffled distinct single points 1..N (closed form N(N+1)/2); neither expected output is generated by the reference. Four negative controls respectively ignore toggling, omit the right end of the closed interval, output the count instead of the index sum, and truncate the result to 32 bits; each must exit normally on all formal cases to count as killed.
